basis: Malignant monocytic proliferation involving blood and bone marrow; no additional organ damage established at the required frequency.
Disordered porphyrin metabolism; cutaneous and neurologic damage vary across subtypes and are not universal across this umbrella.
Malignant T-cell lymphoma; haematologic origin and lymphoma mechanism apply. No specific extranodal organ meets the involvement threshold.
Leber congenital amaurosis is an inherited retinal dystrophy causing severe visual loss.
Hypertension with renal and hepatic dysfunction among defining criteria; thrombocytopenia is a major severe-feature criterion. Pulmonary/CNS features omitted under the four-axis cap.
Malignancy of steroid-producing Leydig cells, the endocrine component of the gonad; metastatic sites are not defining organ involvement.
Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor arising from cutaneous nerves; nerve origin determines the axis.
Congenital CMV; intellectual disability, hearing loss and blood/coagulation abnormalities each 30-79% in HPO. Frequent hepatic injury and chorioretinitis omitted under the cap.
Benign epithelial neoplasm arising in a bronchus or lung parenchyma.
Cerebral white-matter disease with temporal cysts and severe developmental impairment; hearing impairment is only occasional.
Tumor originates in the vagina, a reproductive organ outside the axes; mesenchymal histology does not establish locomotor involvement.
Severe granulocyte depletion; the supplied definition explicitly establishes autoimmune causation.
Acute myeloid malignancy involving blood and marrow; RUNX1 mutation does not establish additional organ involvement.
Hereditary fibrous overgrowth of gingiva; gums belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Inherited platelet-lineage disorder. Despite high HPO frequencies, thrombosis and cerebral ischemia are separately diagnosed vascular complications; pruritus causes no intrinsic skin damage.
Adenoma originates in the anterior pituitary endocrine gland; visual or neurologic compression is not established as common.
Placental trophoblastic disorder outside the axes; vomiting is a symptom and hyperthyroidism is an uncommon, separately diagnosed complication.
Nitrogen oxides cause direct toxic pneumonitis and alveolar injury. The supplied hypersensitivity wording is misleading for this chemical inhalation disease.
Localized cholesterol accumulation changes the gallbladder wall; gallbladder belongs to the hepatic axis. No systemic metabolic disorder is established.
Chronic inflammation of CNS meninges; this etiologically broad concept does not establish an infectious or autoimmune mechanism.
Adenocarcinoma originates in urinary bladder epithelium; the renal axis includes the bladder.
IgE-mediated allergy to alpha-gal; episodic urticaria, gastrointestinal symptoms and anaphylaxis do not establish persistent organ damage.
Benign neoplasm occupies the pericardium, which belongs to the cardiovascular axis.
NPM1-mutated acute myeloid malignancy of blood and marrow; monocytic differentiation does not establish another affected organ.
Protozoal infection directly inflames and damages intestinal mucosa, causing dysentery.
